newsitem.title: UK: U.S. funds keen on Treasuries, reducing equities.
newsitem.headline: U.S. funds keen on Treasuries, reducing equities.

text.p: U.S. fund managers are keen buyers of U.S. Treasuries and are looking to reduce their weighting in domestic equities, a February survey by Merrill Lynch released on Monday shows.
Among U.S.-based managers, buyers of Treasuries outnumbered sellers by 19 percent, while sellers were outnumbering buyers by 15 percent in U.S. equities.
"The level of buying is similar to that in late 1994, prior to the strong rally in bond prices," the survey said.

It was carried out in early February by Gallup among 47 institutions, and said sentiment in equities continued to rise in favour of the technology sector. Managers had become less bullish on the financial sector.
It noted U.S. fund managers were less interested in Continental Europe, saw some selling in UK equities and found Japanese equities back in favour.
Latin American and Pacfic Basin equities were also being bought.
U.S. managers were no longer raising cash holdings, and were keen buyers of domestic bonds.
Japanese managers turned buyers of U.S. equities in February, it said, while European and UK managers were sellers.
